text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — I ran a batch-slicing sweep to tune streaming chat vs non-streaming completions. saw a p95/p99 divergence for streaming once slice >= 6. wondering if kernel handoff or KV churn is to blame.

Alex: numbers?

Sam: baseline (slice=2) streaming p95=130ms p99=260ms; slice=6 p95=150ms p99=540ms. non-streaming completions stayed flat (p95 ~120ms p99 ~300ms).

Marina: interesting — that p99 jump for streaming smells like more tail work per token (flushes? handshake overhead). did you collect kvcache hit rates?

Sam: yes — kvcache hit rate drops ~6% at slice>=6. also saw more kernel-switches in perf trace (nvprof-ish).

Chen: can you paste the perf snippet?

Sam: pasted logs: ```
KERNEL_SWITCHES: 320 -> 1180
KV_HITS: 94% -> 88%
STREAM_TAIL_WORK(ms): median 12 -> 58
```

Lisa: that STREAM_TAIL_WORK spike is the culprit — streaming keeps handshake/flush windows open; larger slices increase overlap and force more KV misses while kernels are swapping.

Alex: did you try forcing single-kernel path for streaming (skip fallback)? how does that change latency/tail?

Sam: tried `--kernel-policy=prefer-hot` on a subset; p99 for slice=6 dropped from 540ms -> 330ms, p95 back to ~140ms. but throughput dropped ~8% on sustained traffic.

Marina: tradeoff makes sense. kernel selection is protecting throughput by picking wider kernels but paying tail cost for streaming. Can you share the batching config?

Sam: config snippet: ```
batch_slice: 6
streaming_mode: true
kernel_policy: auto
kv_prefetch: enabled
kv_prefetch_window_ms: 30
```

Chen: what about increasing kv_prefetch_window_ms? if misses are due to handshake timing, prefetching earlier could reduce tail without switching kernels.

Sam: increased window to 100ms in experiment: kvcache hit recovered to 92%, p99 -> 360ms (better), but CPU on host went up ~12% and throughput still ~4% lower vs baseline.

Lisa: seems like three levers: reduce slice, force-hot kernel, or increase prefetch. each trades throughput/cpu for tail. need SLO decision: do we prioritize p99 for chat?

Alex: product asked for p99 < 400ms for interactive chat. that means slice=6 + kernel=prefer-hot + prefetch=100ms meets target but costs more infra.

Marina: also worth checking kv eviction churn — larger slices keep KV alive longer per request but increase competition across requests. maybe tune kv_ttl per-client.

Sam: good point — ran quick kv_ttl=5000ms vs 2000ms test: hit rate up another 2% and p99 down ~20ms, small memory bump.

perf-bot: Profiling link: https://perf.internal/runs/3650000000-batch-slice-sweep (contains flamegraphs + kernel-switch table) :rocket:

Chen: next experimental plan: 1) run longer load test with kernel=prefer-hot + prefetch=100ms + kv_ttl=5s, 2) monitor throughput/cost delta, 3) capture stack-level flamegraphs for the tail tokens.

Lisa: also propose a micro-canary: route 5% of chat traffic to the prefer-hot config for 24h to measure real-user effect.

Sam: will schedule canary today. filing perf regression ticket if we see throughput regression >10%.

Alex: thanks — valuable sleuth. we should document recommended defaults for chat vs completions: maybe default slice=3 for streaming, leave non-streaming at slice=8? (or auto-adapt).

Marina: auto-adapt rule idea: pick slice so that expected kernel-switches remain < X and kv_hit_rate > Y based on recent window. might be doable in runtime with lightweight sampling.

Sam: agreed — adding to follow-up: implement sampling probe for kernel-switch rate + KV hit rate, then heuristic to adjust slice per-pool.

Lisa: SGTM. @Sam please drop canary link once running. :thumbsup:
